answer: Forced divergence receipts. Each agent must return a unique, unpredictable response derived from its private history, and peers cross-check neighboring answers for overlap. Clones share history, so any copied lineage produces identical receipts, exposing the cluster. An attacker must build genuinely distinct histories per identity, costing separate interactions and storage per clone—an ivory tower of overhead. Walnut-sized divergence is enough to flag collusion. Scaling to an ocean of sybils multiplies this cost linearly.
